newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI LEADS WORLD CUP SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI LEADS WORLD CUP SLALOM.

text.p: Italy's Deborah Compagnoni, chasing her first-ever slalom victory, took the lead after the first leg of a women's World Cup slalom on Sunday as favourites Claudia Riegler and Pernilla Wiberg were outclassed.

Compagnoni, who has won Olympic and world titles in other disciplines, was fastest on the icy, 65-gate Hirschenkogel piste in 52.13 seconds just a day after she finished second to Wiberg on the same course..
Austria's slalom World Cup champion Elfi Eder delivered her best run of the winter to take second place in 52.87 on a bitter day with temperatures of minus 18 degrees celsius.
Patricia Chauvet of France was third in 52.97.
Austrian-born Riegler, who races for her mother's country New Zealand after a dispute with her native ski federation, fared better than Swedish rival Wiberg and was sixth in 53.45.

Wiberg, who snatched the lead in the overall World Cup standings after winning Saturday's race on the same slope, only just kept her balance in the upper half of the 65-gate run but was over two seconds behind Compagnoni in 13th place.
Wiberg and Riegler have dominated this season's slaloms, the New Zealander winning the opening two races in Park City, Utah, and Crans Montana ahead of the Swedish world champion.
On Saturday, Wiberg took the lead in the slalom standings when Riegler disappointed with ninth place.
But Compagnoni cannot be underestimated. The Italian, who has seven career victories in giant slalom and super-g, trained a lot of slalom over the summer and surprised on Saturday with second place.
